definition: A visualization technique that highlights which parts of an input (such as regions of an image) most strongly influenced a model's output.
details: Saliency maps are commonly used in computer vision to provide intuitive, visual explanations of what a model 'focused on' when making a particular classification or decision.
story: Picture walking through a crowd and instantly picking out a familiar face without reading a single name tag. Boil it down and it is this: A visualization technique that highlights which parts of an input (such as regions of an image) most strongly influenced a model's output. Here is why it matters: Saliency maps are commonly used in computer vision to provide intuitive, visual explanations of what a model 'focused on' when making a particular classification or decision. Sight, for a machine, is a long climb from raw light to a name. That pixel-to-meaning climb is Saliency Map.
